PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.

scenes.heading: EXT. CEMETERY - LATE DAY - FLASHBACK (”PIE-LETTE” RE-USE)

lines.text: An expansive hillside graveyard filled with headstones.
At this very moment, in the town of Coeur
d’Coeurs...
ON ONE SIDE
YOUNG CHUCK is flanked by 30-something AUNTS VIVIAN AND LILY,
looking into an open grave as a RABBI reads from a prayer book.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...a girl named Chuck was attending her
father’s funeral. The only parent she had
ever known was accidentally, inadvertently
killed by the boy she loved...
ON THE OTHER SIDE
YOUNG NED and his FATHER look into an open grave as a PRIEST
reads from a prayer book.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...who was, at this very moment, attending his own
mother’s funeral, who had actually died twice.

scenes.heading: INT. YOUNG NED’S CHILDHOOD KITCHEN - DAY (”PIE-LETTE” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned’s MOTHER sweeps the dirt off his clothes, then
abruptly DROPS OUT OF FRAME mid-sweep.
It was a blood vessel bursting in her brain
that caused Ned’s mother’s first death.
Young Ned turns to find his mother dead on the linoleum floor.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
However, Young Ned had a secret gift: he could
touch dead things and bring them back to life.
He touches her cheek and we see a BOLT OF STATIC ELECTRICITY.
His mother blinks and sits up.
NED’S MOTHER
I must’ve slipped. Clumsy.
(then)
Did the timer go off?
It was a gift with two simple caveats:
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Young Ned watches her get to her feet, brush off her apron and
check the pie in the oven.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Keep a dead thing alive for more than a minute
and something else would die in its place.
THROUGH THE KITCHEN WINDOW, we SEE Chuck’s father drop dead in
his yard as he’s watering the lawn.
Ned’s mother GASPS as she sees Chuck’s father dead in the yard.
SMASH, the pie plate she’s holding SHATTERS to the ground.

scenes.heading: INT. YOUNG NED’S CHILDHOOD BEDROOM - NIGHT (”PIE-LETTE” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned’s mother pulls up the blankets so he can slide into
bed. She draws the blanket up to his chin...
And touch a dead thing twice, it dies again,
this time forever.
...and kisses him on the forehead, FLASHING DEAD AGAIN and
dropping out of frame. Young Ned hops out of bed and kneels
next to his dead mother, poking her cheek, waiting for her to
open her eyes again. She doesn’t. OFF Ned... MATCH CUT TO:
As before. Young Ned stares at his mother’s open grave and
glances at Young Chuck, who is staring at him.
Young Ned felt responsible not only for his
mother’s death, but the death of Chuck’s father.
His feelings of guilt were amplified...
Young Ned and Young Chuck ENTER FRAME from their respective
sides, silhouetted by the sun.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...because he, too, was in love.
They kiss. And then Chuck walks away. Ned watches her go.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The next time Young Ned would see the girl
named Chuck she would be dead.

scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - DAY (”DUMMY” RE-USE)

lines.text: Ned’s father pats him on the shoulder and walks away.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
Unlike Chuck, Young Ned still had a father, but
after a brief mourning period, he would deposit
Ned at the Longborough School for Boys.

scenes.heading: EXT. CHUCK’S CHILDHOOD HOME - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: YOUNG CHUCK stares at the spot on the lawn where her father
died. A BEE flits past Chuck’s nose and she follows it with her
eyes, turning to see AUNTS LILY and VIVIAN, wearing beekeeper’s
suits, standing next to a collection of box hives.
After her own father’s death, Chuck was
fostered by Aunts Lily and Vivian, a renown
synchronized swimming duo and sister
neurotics, who helped her build a new home...
CLOSE ON - A NEWSPAPER AD
It reads: “Bee-lieve in the Power of Bees! As seen in the
Thrifty Nickel!”
...bee-by-bee.
CAMERA PULLS OUT TO REVEAL THE NEWSPAPER AD is a sticker on the
side of a LARGE, COMMERCIAL BOX that’s been recently opened.
Lily stands next to it, uncomfortable with the sentiment.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was Aunt Lily who found the ad on the back
pages of the “Thrifty Nickel,” in a fleeting
wisp of something resembling maternal instinct.
Just wanted you to stop staring at that spot
where your father died. It’s obsessive.
REVEAL smiling Young Chuck, dressed in a child-sized beekeeper’s
suit, reading a manual entitled: “Bee Basics from A-to-BZZZZ.”
Young Chuck rebuilt her home by building a new
home for a homeless Queen and her hive. The
bees thrived. So did Chuck.

scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - DAY (”DUMMY” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned stands in front of the same suitcases, as before.
And while Chuck thrived, Ned waited for his
father to bring him home... and waited...
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - SUNSET (”DUMMY” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned stands in front of the same suitcases.
...and waited...

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - NIGHT (”DUMMY” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned stand with his suitcases as the CRICKETS CHIRP.

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL - KITCHEN (”SMELL OF SUCCESS” RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Ned ENTERS and approaches the TOASTER, where he sees a
reflection of his mother offering up a freshly-baked pie.
Just as Chuck remembered how home felt...
LATER: Young Ned pulls his own freshly-baked pie out of the oven.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Ned tried not to forget what home was. He
held onto it the only way he could...
As YOUNG NED MORPHS INTO ADULT NED, we are...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and became the Pie-Maker.
CAMERA PULLS OUT FROM ADULT NED REVEALING THE PIE HOLE.
CHUCK’s body splashes into the water.
And the girl named Chuck... became dead. She
was 28 years, 24 weeks, 3 days, 11 hours and 51
minutes old when murdered on a Tahitian getaway.
NED runs up to the two graveyard workers about to shovel the
first shovelful of dirt onto Chuck’s coffin.
But one touch from the Pie-Maker...
Hey, I think somebody’s truck’s on fire.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
They look over their shoulders to see their work truck CONSUMED
IN FLAMES. The workers gasp and run to put out the fire. Ned
makes sure they’re not looking and opens Chuck’s coffin lid.
...and she was alive once more.
Sorry I’m late.
The Pie-Maker could never touch her again.
Chuck’s survival now depended on a delicate
dance... a ballet of avoidance.
CHUCK crosses, passing NED, who then crosses and passes Chuck.
Ned shuffles by, wearing corduroy pants and slippers with bells.
The Pie-Maker took precautions to ensure Chuck
felt safe at home. Slippers were worn, adorned
with bells. Corduroy was always recommended.
As Chuck crosses an intersection of furniture, Ned waits, Chuck
stops, Ned goes about his path, tying his tie:
Crossing. Waiting.
Stopping. Going.
DIGBY’s head bobs to-and-fro, like he’s watching a tennis match.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Digby kept his eyes open to the hazards of
touch, a canine proximity alert who could not
only play dead...
QUICK POP - FIELD OF DAISIES (RE-USE FROM “PIE-LETTE”)
Digby runs into the road and is promptly hit by a passing semi.
...but could do so from experience.
RESUME
Ned scratches Digby’s neck with his handheld petting device.
Chuck approaches Ned just as he’s about to turn right into her.
Digby BARKS, preventing a near-collision.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
Neither the Pie-Maker nor Chuck could move
without the other one knowing. And to the Pie-
Maker, it felt like home.
CLOSE ON BEEHIVE
So Chuck and the Pie-Maker built a home
together... bee-by-bee.
CAMERA CONTINUES PULLING BACK until we are--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Tragically, rogue pesticides killed those bees...

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - MORNING

lines.text: It’s a beautiful morning. Ned stands bare-chested, in his
boxers and socks, and Chuck’s wearing the most adorable undies
you’ve ever seen, both surrounded by hives and all sorts of
flowers. Chuck looks inside a hive.
...but only briefly.
This’ll go better if you wear less clothes.
I’ve already been shucked like an ear of corn.
(flirtatiously closer)
I’m shucked, too. All the way to my silky
intimates just to put on a beekeeper’s suit.
Why are you shucked and silky?
It seemed only fair.
Ned finally pulls off his socks and tosses them aside. Chuck
pulls up her beekeeper’s suit over her shoulders and zips.
You stopped being fair.
Chuck smiles, puts on her helmet and veil.
You do realize I can get new bees. I can make
a new home for new bees.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
I like this bee home the way it is -- was.
You love these bees. A happy hive is a happy
home and you can’t be happy if you’re dead.
There are a thousand dead bees here. I don’t
want a thousand butterflies to die because you
brought my bees back to life.
Think of it as a pest-control issue. There’s
an infestation of water bugs in the drain
pipes and if I touch a thousand little dead
bees back to life, then maybe a thousand
little water bugs will no longer be a problem.
Last time when I asked you to bring something
back to life, you said no.
It was your dad. That woulda’ been weird. If
not actively traumatic.
I don’t know. To have my dad back if even for
a minute. It may be ghoulish, yes, but also
sweet. Like a taxidermied pet or putting
someone’s ashes in a teddy bear. Wouldn’t you
wanna have your dad back... if you could...
even for a minute?
That would be an awkward minute. I haven’t seen
or heard from the man in twenty years. I’ll
stick to bees; least they know what home is.
She grabs an inactive hive filled with dead bees and climbs a
low dais, standing over nearly-naked Ned.
This is very sweet of you.
And will probably sting.
Just don’t offend the bees.
How would I offend the bees?
But she’s already tipping the hive. Ned plugs his ears and
closes his eyes as Chuck pours bees.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED: (2)
EACH BEE FLASHES WITH LIFE as they make contact with his bare
skin. FLASH-FLASH-FLASH-FLASH-FLASH -- the alive-again bees
LIGHT-UP like firecrackers.
Digby BARKS as they bounce off Ned, flying toward the flowers
around the hive. A bee FLASHES ALIVE on Ned’s torso and flies
right into his arm, FLASHING DEAD and dropping to the ground.
CAMERA FINDS A DRAINAGE PIPE where DEAD WATER BUGS pour out.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - DAY

lines.text: OLIVE moves from booth to booth, serving pies to customers.
Olive Snook once felt as at home in her Pie
Hole uniform as she did her own skin. But
recently, home and uniform had begun to chafe.
Olive unloads the last of the pies and scratches under her
uniform. She turns to see her CUSTOMER staring at Chuck, who
ENTERS with Ned and crosses to the kitchen.
Doesn’t she look like that “Lonely Tourist”
girl who got killed on a Tahitian getaway?
No, not at all. Actually, wasn’t that girl
Asian? Hey, you want a box for that, to-go?
Believing Chuck merely faked her death, Olive
kept the secret that Chuck was still alive.
Olive turns to see Ned rolling dough at his preparation table.
He looks up and smiles at her, she swoons.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But the secret that weighed the most in
Olive’s satchel of deception was that she was
still in love with the Pie-Maker.
POPPING UP INTO FRAME is a finished POP-UP ILLUSTRATION of a
little girl in pigtails, stroking her chin. We are--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
At that very moment, Private Investigator
Emerson Cod was enjoying a new love of the
pop-up variety.
EMERSON COD sits at his desk, working over his nearly-completed
POP-UP BOOK. He pulls a tab and the little girl raises a
magnifying glass to her eye (which appears to magnify).
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
Combining his fondness of detective work and
stress knitting, Mr. Cod authored and
constructed “Lil’ GumShoe.”
REVEAL the cover and title: “LIL’ GUMSHOE by EMERSON COD.”
I love you, “Lil’ GumShoe.”
Mr. Cod had time to author pop-ups because he
saved time solving murders with a Pie-Maker who
can undead the dead and ask how they got that way.
Emerson turns the pages of his pop-up creation, smiling.
Suddenly, his office door SWINGS OPEN. An emotional man of
about 30, named DUSTY FITZ, stands in the doorway.
My wife has been murdered.
What do the Po-Po got to say about your wife
being murdered, Mr. Fitz?
Work-related mishap. Said she was sloppy.
Was she sloppy?
She wasn’t sloppy. She was having an affair.
Said she was gonna leave me or him. Not sure
which. She wasn’t using proper nouns, but the
caller ID said she was talking to someone at
Betty’s Bees. Thank God I was eavesdropping.
If your old lady was stepping out on you, why
do you care who killed her?
I’m hoping she was leaving him and not me. I
couldn’t bear it if she was leaving me.
Uh-huh. What line of work was she in?
Bees. Know anything about bees?
Emerson heaves an exhausted sigh.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (2)
I know somebody who knows somebody.
(then)
Before we continue, I’d like to say I’m sorry
for your loss and... I do accept credit cards.
Emerson slaps a credit card slider on his desk.
I have a check card.
Any ladle’s sweet that dishes out gravy.
The facts were these:
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON KENTUCKY FITZ (late-20s) in her Betty’s Bees
uniform, sitting in front of the corporate logo.
One Kentucky Fitz, wife of Dusty, was the
number-one Bee-Girl of Betty’s Bees.
QUICK FLASHES OF BETTY’S BEES PRODUCT LINE FROM THE CATALOG:
Creams, soaps, shampoos, lip balms, all sporting Betty Bee’s mug.
Betty’s Bees (trademark) was all the buzz in
beauty and well-being with honey and honey-
based moisturizers, anti-aging creams, soaps
and lip balms.
CAMERA MOVES WITH THE CORONER as he leads Ned, Emerson and Chuck
to two COVERED BODIES on two tables, one faceup, one facedown.
Kentucky was 26 years, 3 weeks, 5 days and 39
minutes old when found stung to death behind
the wheel of her Betty’s Bees Bee-mobile.
Which one is Kentucky Fitz?
Biscuits.
“Biscuits”?
The coroner indicates the facedown body first, then faceup.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
You got biscuits, you got shrimps.
(points to heels)
Biscuits.
(points to toes)
Shrimps.
You got something we can use to flip her over?
Why you gotta flip her over? Front don’t look
much different than the back. And it ain’t
like you gonna be having a conversation.
The coroner holds out his hand, waiting for payment.
It sure ain’t.
Emerson slaps a wad of cash in the coroner’s hand and he EXITS.
Ned touches Kentucky’s shoulder and she FLASHES ALIVE, still
facedown. Her eyes open.
Hello, Kentucky. We’d like to have a
conversation.
Maybe she’s paralyzed from all the bee-stings.
I’m just taking in my surroundings.
Apparently, I’m dead.
Kentucky turns over on the table, knocking the sheet covering
her to the floor, REVEALING her once-beautiful body, now BUBBLED
AND SWOLLEN from thousands of bee-stings. [NOTE: Her naughty
bits will be strategically covered, Austin Powers-style.]
There’s an awkward moment where they all stare at her.
KENTUCKY (CONT’D)
Really?
Chuck quickly grabs the sheet and drapes it back over Kentucky.
Sorry about that. And I’m sorry we have to
pepper you with questions in your last moments
of life, but was your death an accident?
Was I accidentally swarmed by bees? No. That
was on purpose.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED: (2)
Why would someone swarm you with bees?
I may have been up to some mischief.
Your husband thinks what got you killed was a
workplace romance gone all sorts of sour.
My husband has a problem with eavesdropping.
There was no romance. It was my workplace
that went sour. I was leaving Betty’s Bees.
Dusty will be tickled you weren’t cheating.
I love my husband. I could never hurt him.
I’m his only family. He was never close with
his own family and my family doesn’t like him.
So it really is just me. Was just me.
You tell your husband you were leaving Betty’s Bees?
If I told him I was quitting Betty’s Bees,
he’d worry and ask lots of questions why, then
I’d have to lie about sabotaging Betty’s Bees.
Why’d you sabotage Betty’s Bees?
Why? Because Betty deserved it. Intention
was to quit before I got caught.
Who caught you?
I couldn’t see his face. Or her face.
Regardless of genitalia, I didn’t see much.
All the lights went out one by one. Then
there was a terrible hum. And out of the
darkness... out of the night, it came for me.
It spit something, then a swarm of bees
attacked. I tried to get a good look at it,
but the bees were already stinging my eyes.
Ned’s been totally sucked into the story.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED: (3)
That’s terrifying.
(to Chuck and Emerson)
That’s terrifying.
(off watch BEEP)
Oh. Sorry. Five seconds.
Any last wishes? How were you sabotaging--
But Chuck was louder.
My only wish is that Dusty not be alone. He
doesn’t like alone.
Yeah, yeah. How were you sabotaging Betty’s Bees?
With a lot of might--
Ned can’t wait another second. He touches her mid-sentence and
she FLASHES DEAD, but her chest heaves slightly. Emerson shoots
Chuck a look, annoyed.
That’s nice. Don’t know what she was doing,
but we know it required a lot of effort.
Do you hear something?
Is she still breathing?
That’s not breathing.
Kentucky does one last heave and her jaw drops open, BELCHING A
SWARMING CLOUD OF BEES into the room.
Emerson, Chuck and Ned rush in, slamming the door behind them.
The coroner stares:
I told you not to turn her over.
OFF that...
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
Ned, Emerson and Chuck in a booth. Olive bustles back and
forth, eavesdropping as she goes, waiting on various customers.
Could that have happened to me? On the roof?
Could I have been swarmed? In my underwear,
too. I could’ve been swarmed in my underwear.
You don’t just get to put those pictures in my
head. That is an assault on my imagination.
Poor Kentucky. What a horrible way to die.
Thousands of little stingers stinging you.
Olive arrives with two slices of pie, one à la mode, one not.
Like little stinging secrets that don’t just
sting you once, they keep stinging you until
you’re bloated and filled with pus.
(off their stares)
Who wanted à la mode?
Emerson and Chuck raise their hands and Olive places the pies
down in front of them, giving the mode to Emerson and moving on.
Kentucky got bloated and filled with pus on
account of her sabotaging Betty’s Bees.
Boy, Kentucky sure had it out for Betty. But
who had it out for Kentucky?
The Terrifying Bee-Man.
What if he’s made entirely out of bees and the
reason she didn’t see his face is because he
doesn’t have one? What if there’s a whole
society of Bee-Folk who walk among us shaped
like people?
You’re thinking about how you can train
your bees to walk around in people shapes,
aren’t you?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED:
Yes.
Ain’t no bees walking around in people shapes.
Kentucky was wiggity-wiggity-whacked.
With a swarm of bees.
Smells like an inside job.
Kentucky was talking to someone at Betty’s
Bees when Dusty was dropping eaves.
Someone who might know what she was doing and
who would wanna kill her for it.
If it’s an inside job, we need an Inside Bee-Girl.
No.
We’ve got to tap this honey at its source.
Emerson produces a newspaper with a circled ad that reads:
“Calling All Bee-Girls! Bee All You Can Bee with Betty’s Bees.”
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Calling all Bee-Girls.
Under the nom de plume of Kathryn “Kitty”
Pimms, Chuck answered the call calling
for Bee-Girls.
CLOSE ON RÉSUMÉ:
The name on top reads: “Kathryn ‘Kitty’ Pimms.” Chuck’s alias.
ON CHUCK
Dressed for her job interview, hat and bee broach, et. al.
I love bees because they’ve been who they are
without apology for 35 million years. They
don’t have to prey on others to survive. They
work tirelessly, not for themselves but for
each other. They have the freedom to fly out
into the world, yet they always come home.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
Chuck recites her essay as CAMERA PULLS BACK to REVEAL we are--

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - WOOLSEY NICHOLLS’S OFFICE - DAY

lines.text: Chuck sits opposite WOOLSEY NICHOLLS, a jolly man (40s/50s), who
is ENCHANTED with the charming young lady in front of him.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
They have heart and nobility and furry behinds.
Stupendous! You know, I often find that the
most amazing creatures have furry behinds.
He continues to prattle MOS as CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Chuck:
Sitting in Woolsey Nicholls’s office,
discussing the furry behinds of bees, Chuck
realized this was her very first job
interview. Ever. She considered this fact
for a moment, then had to ask:
I have to ask. Are you the Woolsey Nicholls
behind Bzzzzzzzzz! Honey and More?
I am!
What are you doing at Betty’s Bees? Aren’t
you Betty’s Bees’ biggest rival?
I own Betty’s Bees now. We’ve kept the
acquisition very quiet. These days, mergers
can send brand loyalists into a tizzy.
I’m a honey loyalist, you’ll get no tizzy from
me. I just hope you’re not killing Bee-Girls.
I beg your pardon?
The Bee-Girl sales division. With any
acquisition, there’s restructuring and
downsizing. I just hope it doesn’t affect the
Bee-Girls.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED: (2)
Bee-Girls will always have a home in my hive.
Unfortunately, though fortunately for you,
we’ve recently had an opening in our Bee-Girl
division.
I did hear something about Kentucky Fitz.
Something about a honey-harvesting tragedy?
Yes. Very sad. She had a bright future ahead
of her here at the new Betty’s Bees.
I heard someone saying something about
Kentucky planning to leave Betty’s Bees before
she died.
You sure do hear a lot of things.
It’s a very gossipy office.
Well, I believe that particular rumor to be
false, Kitty. Kentucky was invested.
Woolsey pulls out a mock-up of a Betty’s Bees product, featuring
Betty’s original face, and folds over a transparency that covers
Betty’s original face with Kentucky Fitz’s smiling face.
WOOLSEY (CONT’D)
She was the new face of Betty’s Bees. We
designed our entire brand relaunch around her.
But Betty’s the face of Betty’s Bees.
Betty was the old face. “Old” being the
operative word.
She’s 37.
She’s 38. And 38 rounds up to 40, which rounds
up to 50, which rounds up to “old.” And if
you’re in the business of selling products that
promise youth, beauty and vitality, you have to
make a strong case for it. Correction, we have
to make a strong case for it. Kitty, I’d be
honored if you called Betty’s Bees your new home.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED: (3)
Betty’s Bees is my new home.
Stupendous!
Chuck never lets her smile drop. But as we ZOOM in on her BEE
BROACH, we see: the TINY WIRE where the stinger should be.
TIGHT ON ANOTHER WIRE, leading to a pair of old-school
HEADPHONES, currently being shared by Ned and Emerson. Ned
shoots Emerson an annoyed look.
Chuck has a new home. I blame you.
I blame me, too. That went well.
Emerson Cod’s inside man, aka, Betty’s Bees’
newest Bee-Girl Kitty Pimms, buzzed through
the offices of Betty’s Bees...

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - KENTUCKY FITZ’S OFFICE

lines.text: Chuck ENTERS and slinks over to Kentucky’s desk and begins
looking over her datebook before stuffing it under her arm.
...until she buzzed upon the office of one
Kentucky Fitz.
She opens a succession of drawers and realizes the lock on a
particular drawer has been broken. She opens the drawer to see an
ANTIQUE HOUSE KEY with a distinctive bee handle, marked “88.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Chuck-slash-Kitty searched for any hint of a
saboteur’s agenda.
Chuck moves to a closet and opens it and STARTLES TO SEE BETTY
BEE (late 30s) standing inside, STARTLING to see Chuck.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
What she found was the eponymous Betty Bee.
What are you doing in there?
Cognitive therapy for claustrophobia.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
You’re Betty Bee.
Betty steps out of the closet, brushing off her garment.
That’s right. Why am I explaining myself to
you? You should be explaining yourself to me.
I’m sorry. I was told this office was vacant.
(offers her hand)
Kitty Pimms. I was just hired.
By whom?
Woolsey Nicholls.
(concealing disdain)
Woolsey.
(eyes narrow)
So you’re replacing Kentucky? A little soon
after her death. Seems distasteful, doesn’t it?
It does, but it also speaks to the efficiency
of your human resources department.
Betty sizes Chuck up and down as she slides by the desk,
surreptitiously sliding the drawer open and stealing the key.
I wonder how else you’ll be replacing Kentucky.
Since I’m a withered hag tattered by every grain
of sand in the hourglass, Betty’s Bees still
needs a fresh, young face. And after what
happened to Kentucky... well, no one wants to
think about that when they buy lip balm.
Betty moves off, then stops and forces a smile:
BETTY (CONT’D)
Welcome to Betty’s Bees.
Chuck looks down to see the ANTIQUE KEY is now missing.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - BETTY’S OFFICE - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: Betty approaches her desk, opens a drawer, places the antique
key inside and closes and locks the drawer. She looks up and
STARTLES to see Chuck standing just inside her doorway.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED:
I just wanted to say what an honor it is to be
working with you.
Thank you. Get out.
And so Chuck got out, but the question
remained:
Chuck presses dough into a pan as Emerson and Ned stand nearby.
Olive ENTERS and EXITS the scene, coming and going with dirty
plates and pie, respectively.
Betty Bee. Co-conspirator or killer?
Stealing a key out of a dead lady’s desk
doesn’t make you either.
Hide what you know. I’m always hiding what I
know. And Betty’s hiding something by hiding
that key.
Olive’s right. The key is key.
And when I get done serving these pies, I’ll
tell you exactly what that key is for.
Don’t be yapping like you know what you’re
yapping about.
Olive moves off, balancing three slices of pie on her arm.
Kentucky was going to be the new face of
Betty’s Bees, which does give Betty motive.
Getting replaced by younger and better-looking
always gives you motive.
But Kentucky was sabotaging Betty’s Bees
(trademark). Which is owned by Woolsey
Nicholls, which gives Woolsey motive.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
Woolsey’s a businessman. Somebody sabotage
him, he’d send a swarm of lawyers, not bees.
Olive returns with dirty dishes.
I got it. They were lovers of the same-sex
persuasion and the key is for their love nest.
We’ve ruled out workplace romance.
I’ll just cross that off my list then.
I haven’t ruled out workplace romance.
Romance gives you motive. Somebody’s always
loving somebody they shouldn’t be loving.
Olive notices Emerson was starting right at her when he said it.
She shoots him a look and turns her attention to Chuck, who
surreptitiously uncaps the dropper bottle and doses the pie.
(re: the pie)
Is that for your aunts?
Mmm-hmm. Extra vanilla.
Aunt Lily loves her vanilla.

scenes.heading: EXT. AUNTS’ HOUSE - WINTER NIGHT (RE-USE FROM “CORPSICLE”)

lines.text: Olive Snook discovered it wasn’t vanilla while
delivering pie to Chuck’s aunts. It wasn’t
the only secret she would discover that night.

scenes.heading: INT. AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM (RE-USE FROM “CORPSICLE”)

lines.text: A MERMAID floats right before Lily’s eye, at least appears to.
The high doses of herbal mood-enhancers not
only caused particularly-vivid side effects,
but they also prompted a confession:
I’m Charlotte’s mother.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 22.
CONTINUED:
Lily blinks and the mermaid is now Olive. Olive can only stare.
The infamous CHEESE CRAB crawls onto her shoulder and shares
Olive’s stunned disbelief.
It was a confession not even Lily’s sister
Vivian had heard. And to ensure that she never
would, Lily banished Olive from their lives.
Chuck places the pie in a Pie Hole box and hands it to Olive as
she’s crossing into the kitchen.
Since both Chuck and her mother were supposed
to be dead, neither could know the other was
alive.
Olive walks around the corner and throws the pie in the trash.
Chuck joins Emerson on the stools, with Ned behind the counter.
I don’t know if Betty killed Kentucky or
didn’t kill Kentucky, but either way, Betty’s
hiding something about something.
I’ll give Betty the shakedown tomorrow.
No shaking. What if somebody at Betty’s Bees
finds out you’re a spy. Spying is a lot like
sabotage. In that they kill you for it.
That’s what you do with spies and saboteurs.
You kill them and you don’t feel bad about it
because they were spying and sabotaging.
Olive approaches with a dish rag and starts wiping the counter.
They won’t kill me during office hours.
Yeah. Stop trying to spook my inside man.
You could die.
And you’re already dead.
LILY (O.S.)
Told you she wasn’t dead.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 23.
CONTINUED:
Ned, Emerson, Olive and Chuck all turn to see: AUNTS LILY and
VIVIAN ENTER. Ned and Olive stare in horror at Vivian and Lily.
Olive and Ned turn to see: Chuck’s stool is spinning by itself
and Chuck is nowhere in sight, and neither is Emerson.
If I could breathe, I would vomit.
Olive Snook, every week, a delicious, life-
giving pie, then nothing for months. I
thought you were dead. And so soon after
Charlotte. I was beginning to take everyone
dying personally.
We would have called, but by the time I knew
we were coming, Vivian was already on the bus.
Lily was very tenacious. She tried to get me
to come home at six consecutive stops.
She insisted on coming all this way just to
ask why you stopped delivering pie.
I’m... just really flaky.
That’s what I told her.
It’s not about the pie. Although the pie was
always lovely and... so vivid.
I gotta go get somebody’s something.
KITCHEN
Olive ENTERS to find Chuck squatting next to the freezers, as
Emerson looks on. They speak in hushed tones:
You stopped delivering their special pies?
She said, “Months.” All this time I’ve been
making special pies and...
...and dosing them with God-knows-what that
you claim is vanilla but that ain’t vanilla.
Chuck’s mouth drops and Olive spins around with pie box in hand.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 24.
CONTINUED:
What’d you do with the pie I just baked them?
I threw it away.
DINING ROOM
Olive approaches with the pie box and tries to steer around the
aunts and Ned, but Vivian steps right into her path.
The weight of kept secrets had become
unbearable for the pint-sized pie-slinger.
Olive... why won’t you talk to me? I thought
you were my friend.
Like I said, flaky.
I’ve got something to say. And I’m gonna say
it to you, you, you and your hump.
In the kitchen, we can see Emerson skulking toward the back
door, wearing a large trench coat draped over his shoulders
concealing Chuck, who is holding onto him piggyback style.
Olive wanted to let loose the secrets and lies
she’d been force-fed by her friends... that
Chuck was still alive... that Lily was her
mother, but instead what came out was this:
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON OLIVE as she emits a PIERCING SCREAM. Heads
turn. Olive keeps SCREAMING. Ned, Lily and Vivian stare.
Emerson stalks out with Chuck under his coat, Lily and Vivian
are too busy staring at a screaming Olive.
What has gotten into you?
I am a sawed-off shotgun of secrets!
Did she say she was armed?
I don’t have a gun! I am a gun! At any
moment, truth buckshot could come spewing
outta my muzzle! Look out!
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 25.
CONTINUED:
That’s enough. That’s enough.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Truer words have never been spoken. This
rifle is going away in a satin-lined case with
the trigger locked and the safety on. I quit.
I’m quitting you... and this... all of this.
Olive, you don’t have to quit. You just have
to calm down. Would you like a drink? Lily,
hand me your purse.
(to Ned, heart breaking)
I’m not thirsty. I’m tendering my resignation
and resigning my tenders to the cold, harsh
reality of what’s not meant to be.
You can’t just leave.
Vivian, go wait outside.
But...
Haven’t you caused enough trouble?
Vivian reluctantly walks outside. She glances back at Olive.
This is your home. Where you gonna go?
I know a place.
OFF that pronouncement...
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
Ned ENTERS to find Chuck standing in the middle of Olive’s now-
empty apartment. Her furniture, her pictures, her personal
tchotchkes -- all gone. Only plants remain.
Aunt Vivian always used to say there was
nothing sadder than an empty birdcage.
(then)
Is Olive ever coming home?
She didn’t say. Wouldn’t say. She just said
her apartment was paid through the end of the
year and asked me to water her plants.
I feel like I broke her. I enlisted her to spy
on my aunts, then turned her into a homeopathic
drug mule.
What kind of homeopathic drugs was she muling?
I baked antidepressants into pies for my aunts
to try to get them out of the house.
Something I always wanted to do when I was
alive but just never had the opportunity.
Ned stares at her slack-jawed for a moment, then:
Did it work?
It got them out of the house. Well, Olive got
them out of the house. They got out of the
house. Vivian took the bus. She hates the
bus. It’s too intimate. Oh, I wish there was
some way I could thank Olive.
You could water her plants.
I already did. I couldn’t sleep. My mind
wandered over here, then I followed. Then
my mind wandered off again.
Where’d it go?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 27.
CONTINUED:
Home. Home-home. With my dad.
Oh. That’s a ways to wander.
It’s been wandering since Betty’s Bees. You
know, that was my first job interview ever?
For most people, that’s the big foray into
growing up and leaving home. And I didn’t
foray until yesterday.
Leaving home is overrated. But I may be biased.
I haven’t gone anywhere with my life and this
is my second one. All I have is a fake
résumé filled with things I’ve never done.
I’ve never even lived alone. How long did
you live alone?
Long enough.
But don’t you think that’s odd? I find that
odd. My entire life... My aunts swept in
the moment my dad died. You swept in the
moment I died.
You’re thinking about living here now,
aren’t you?
Yes.
(then)
You hate corduroy. And sleigh-bell slippers.
And I’ll stop walking in on you doing things
you don’t want me to know you’re doing.
That never would have happened if you were
wearing your slippers.
I think it’ll be romantic.
I’m confused. More.
“More”?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 28.
CONTINUED: (2)
More of an explanation. How is it romantic?
You got a job and now you’re moving out.
I didn’t get a job. I’m undercover Kitty.
And I’m not moving out. I’m moving next door.
It’s very French. First-class, Parisian
living. His and Her suites and coy midnight
knocks on the door to share a lover’s boudoir.
You’ll be knocking?
Mmm-hmm. You can knock, too.
This was not romantic for the Pie-Maker.
Yay. Knocking.
They turn to see Emerson in the doorway, surveying the room.
Where’s Olive?
CAMERA DESCENDS THROUGH the BANK OF CLOUDS that part to REVEAL
ROCKY, SNOW-COVERED MOUNTAINS.
Olive Snook was where Lily had taken her.
We HEAR A SWELLING ORCHESTRA reminiscent of Rodgers and
Hammerstein, but legally NOT. CAMERA DIPS into a lush valley,
wooded with steep cliffs, soaring over the treetops, REVEALING
an open, green field tucked away between the mountain peaks.
CAMERA FINDS OLIVE SNOOK running over the hill, in Julie Andrews-
“Sister Maria” nun regalia. She spins TOWARD CAMERA, arms
outstretched, opens her mouth and SINGS A BEAUTIFUL ARIA.
SINGING ARIA...
A passing GAGGLE OF NUNS react unfavorably, shushing Olive:
Shhhhh.
It was a place that valued Olive’s silence as
much as Lily did.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 29.
OMIT
The doors bang OPEN TO REVEAL Woolsey with one arm around Chuck,
with his other arm holding a large BINDER. The BANG of the
doors STARTLES Betty sitting behind her desk.
Hello, Betty! A little bee tells me you’ve
met Kitty Pimms.
Briefly.
This morning Kitty says to me, she says, “I
wanna talk to Betty Bee, Bee-Girl to Bee-Girl,
and tell her how much she means to me.”
Bless.
I’ll leave you two ladies to get acquainted.
If there’s a lull in conversation, ask Kitty
why she loves bees. You’ll be glad you did!
Woolsey shuts the doors behind him, with a salute, as Chuck
spots the locked drawer she saw Betty put the key in.
Betty, I know Kentucky was your number-one Bee-
Girl and I’m not looking to replace her, but I
would like to live up to her standard of honey
harvesting and sales excellence.
You’re not really going to stand there and
kiss my ass, are you? Or didn’t Woolsey tell
you? He didn’t. How politic.
Tell me what?
Woolsey’s acquisition was a hostile takeover.
He didn’t mention the “hostile” part.
Oh, yes. The ass you were just kissing is now
just the ass of a retired honey mascot.
That’s my new title. Honey mascot-slash-
Consultant. Used to be Founder and President.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 30.
CONTINUED:
That’d make me stinging mad.
(shrugs)
Eh. I get to keep my old office. Just not my
dignity. When all of your bees die, it’s hard
to care about any of it.
Your bees died?
Finger on the pulse, Kitty. The colony
collapsed. Mites might’ve caused it. In fact,
we know they did. Took over every hive. Not
long after Woolsey took over Betty’s Bees. It’d
almost be poetic if it didn’t suck so much.
Kentucky didn’t sabotage Betty’s Bees with a
lot of might. She sabotaged Betty’s Bees with:
A lot of mite. Ss.
(off Betty’s look)
Take a lotta mites to cause a colony collapse.
Sure does.
(then)
I grew up with generations of those bees.
The first hive was an infestation in the
corner of my bedroom. I was five. I tried
to kill it.
Oh.
I was stopped. Mother was a Methodist and
Daddy was a Pragmatist so “God put those bees
there for a reason.” They were right.
You lived with bees? That sounds magical.
We called it the Honey House. The Honey House
is empty now. We all left together, me and
the bees. Those bees built Betty’s Bees.
What happened to your bees... do you think
that could have been... sabotage?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 31.
CONTINUED: (2)
A conspiracy. How dramatic. You think
someone intentionally murdered my bees?
Just a thought.
If it were sabotage that killed my bees...
let’s just say I wouldn’t want to be the
saboteur. But this wasn’t sabotage, Kitty.
Sometimes bad things just happen.
Unbeknownst to Chuck, aka, Kitty Pimms,
something bad was about to just happen to her.
OFF that...
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.
Ned, Emerson and Chuck sit in a booth with Dusty Fitz.
Kentucky ever say anything about colony
collapse?
Is it upsetting? She tends not to tell me
things that might be upsetting.
It’s when a beehive becomes inhospitable -- in
this case, infested with mites. The bees all
fly away to die. It’s a natural phenomenon.
But when you got a bee company bought out by
its chief rival, and a star employee dead,
maybe it don’t happen so naturally.
Kentucky was sabotaging Betty’s Bees, which
required a lot of might, as in effort, and a lot
of mites, as in pests. She infected the hives.
Somebody found out and they killed her for it.
How do you know she was sabotaging anything?
She confessed. Before she died. Not to us,
but to a reliable source who also wishes to
remain anonymous.
Is your reliable source Betty Bee?
What makes you say that?
Kentucky was very close with Betty. They were
like sisters until someone asked Kentucky to be
the new Betty. Then they didn’t talk anymore.
Kentucky just stopped mentioning her.
Betty stole a bee-handled key from your wife’s
desk. Does that mean anything to you?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 33.
CONTINUED:
If it had a bee handle, it might be from
Betty’s Bees. Kentucky had a safe-deposit box
at the Betty Bee Credit Union.
We need to get that key.
I know it’s hard to hear your wife was killed
because she was a saboteur, but the good news
is she wasn’t cheating on you. She loved you
very much. She would never hurt you.
(fighting emotion)
She was the only family I ever had. That I
liked or that liked me. If I was more
comfortable with you people, I’d cry.
You can cry. It’s okay.
It’s not okay for a grown man to weep in
public with happy families enjoying pie.
(to Dusty, sensitively)
If you can’t hold it, you go to the men’s room
and cry in private on the toilet like a man.
Excuse me.
Dusty quickly moves off. After he’s gone:
I saw where Betty put that key. I can get it
tomorrow. She can’t stay in her office all day.
Emerson and Chuck look to Ned for an argument.
What?
Thought you might start squawking about how
dangerous it is to go back. Squawk-squawk.
I’m not gonna wag my finger, if that’s what
you expect. This is Chuck’s life and she’s
entitled to live it however she’d like. Can’t
expect her to sit inside all day and... HIDE!
I don’t need to--
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 34.
CONTINUED: (2)
Hide your ass, woman.
Vivian approaches the bakery, watching all the blinds being
pulled one after the other and the OPEN sign turned to read:
“CLOSED.” Ned quickly comes outside, spinning and locking the
door behind him. He turns to see Vivian approaching.
Oh. Vivian. I didn’t see you. I was just
closing up. There. All closed.
There are still people inside.
Cleaning crew. How are you?
To be honest, I wasn’t craving pie. I was
craving company. Lily absconded with herself.
First time in 30 years I don’t know where she
is. I didn’t know where else to go.
It’s all right. I’m sure Lily will be back.
Oh, yes. Though I don’t know about Olive...
and then, of course, there’s Charlotte.
Everyone seems to be leaving me. Home was my
haven. Now all the things there just remind
me of all the things not there.
Chuck. I mean, Charlotte.
Her room is how she left it. Clothes in the
closet, books on the shelves. Her special
pillow still at the head of her bed.
I didn’t know she had a special pillow.
It was her father’s. I’m sure it’s teeming
with fungus and microscopic bugs that feed on
flakes of human skin, but she was fond of it.
I know you loved having Charlotte safe at
home, smiling on the other side of the room...
but she’s gone now. She’s moved out.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.
CONTINUED:
(corrects himself)
I mean, on. She’s moved on. Maybe it’s time
for you to move on and get rid of that pillow.
As the Pie-Maker considered Chuck’s worldly
belongings and how Vivian clinged to them...
In the middle of the courtyard, stacked high, are Olive’s
belongings: steamer trunks, her couch, etc. Olive approaches a
stern-yet-serene-looking MOTHER SUPERIOR.
...Olive was clinging to her own.
Excuse me, Mother Superior. I’ve been here
for a day and I was told the porter would come
for my things. Do I need to tell him what
room I’m in?
The “poor,” Sister. The poor will come for
your belongings. Part of your vow of poverty.
I thought that was a temporary vow since I’m
only going to be a temporary nun. Don’t you
have some kind of storage facility?
This is your home for as long as you’re
here, and as long as you’re here, you’ll
live as a nun.
But I like my belongings. That’s why they
belong to me. I wanna be poor in other ways.
We offer sanctuary, but it doesn’t come
without a price. Work hard and you’ll see
results. Commit yourself and you may even
find that you wish to stay.
Like a gym membership? I can cancel anytime?
God in His wisdom has led you here. Take
refuge and hide your secret from the world.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 36.
CONTINUED:
Lord, put your arm around my shoulder and
your hand over my mouth.
Once your baby is born, you can return to the
outside world.
Whoa. Hold that pregnant pause. I’m not with-
child. Unless it’s immaculate conception or I
wore a strange man’s underwear.
I just assumed, based on who brought you here.
This is where Lily came to have Chuck? Lily’s
one of those girls I heard about.
Ah. Here come the poor.
Olive’s face drops as DOZENS OF POOR rush toward her belongings.
Chuck approaches the reception desk outside Betty’s office,
wearing her bee broach. Betty’s SECRETARY is hunched over, back
to Chuck, looking through the filing cabinets behind his desk.
Is Betty in?
The assistant turns to REVEAL IT’S NED.
She’s on a call. Can I take a message?
Ned? What are you doing here?
Filing. Fielding calls. Making coffee.
What happened to Betty’s assistant, Giancarlo?
He had to, um, scoot.
What happened to Giancarlo was this:
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 37.
INSERT
A slice of pie on a plate with a note reading: “From a Secret
Admirer in Accounting.”
After eating a slice of pie from what he
believed was a secret admirer in Accounting...
CLOCK WIPE TO:
The same plate, only the pie is 90% eaten. We HEAR an OFF-
CAMERA stomach GURGLE AND RUMBLE, followed by a MOAN.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Giancarlo experienced what could best be
described as “extreme intestinal distress.”
RESUME - NED AND CHUCK, AS BEFORE
You pruned his pie?
Sent him home with the scoots, then I hid in
human resources, waited for them to call Happy
Time Temp Agency. Then I called Happy Time
Temp Agency, canceled their order and showed
up with a smile and a pleasant attitude.
That is the most romantic thing I’ve ever heard.
CLOSE ON - CHUCK’S BEE BROACH...
Emerson sits in the car, listening to the headphones.
He’s. Stalking. You.
RESUME - NED AND CHUCK
You don’t think I’m stalking you?
I’d be a hypocrite if I judged you for dosing
someone’s pie. Why? Are you stalking me?
That depends. Now that we’re living our new
Parisian lifestyle, does that mean I can’t be
close when danger’s about or afoot?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 38.
CONTINUED:
I do feel safer now that you’re here.
(into bee-broach bug)
Good. Then this isn’t stalking. It’s just
good, old-fashioned chivalry.
Just then, the door to Betty’s office swings open and Betty
steps out, putting on her coat. Chuck ducks behind the filing
cabinet so Betty doesn’t see her speaking to Ned.
Walk with me.
Ned glances back at Chuck as he follows Betty.
BETTY (CONT’D)
Cancel all my appointments. I’m leaving
early. But I’ve got one more thing to do.
Have my car waiting for me downstairs.
She tosses Ned her keys over her shoulder as he tries to keep
up. Chuck watches them go, then quickly walks to Betty’s door.
With the Pie-Maker serving the perfect
distraction...

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - BETTY’S OFFICE - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: Chuck skulks into Betty’s office, closing the door behind her.
As she moves over to Betty’s desk, CAMERA PUSHES IN ON BETTY’S
BALCONY DOOR, slightly ajar. A SINGLE BEE flies inside.
...Chuck bee-lined for the stolen bee-key.
ON CHUCK - She grabs a letter opener off Betty’s desk and starts
prying at the locked drawer. The lock pops off and Chuck slides
the drawer open to REVEAL the bee-handled KEY.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
She found the bee-key exactly where Betty Bee
put it. Then she made an equally-important
discovery of a different kind...
She sees a FRAMED NEWSPAPER CLIPPING on top of the credenza.
It’s YOUNG BETTY standing in front of a clapboard house sporting
a BEE BEARD! CAPTION READS: “Betty Bee’s First Bee Beard.”
We HEAR a low-level HUM that builds to an active BZZZZZZZZZing.
A BEE flies through FRAME. Suddenly, Chuck turns to see:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...before she herself was discovered.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 39.
CONTINUED:
The TERRIFYING BEE-MAN, standing right behind her. His/her face
and much of his/her torso is obscured by a MASS OF CRAWLING,
ANXIOUS BEES. Chuck opens her mouth to scream and...
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - BETTY’S OFFICE - DAY

lines.text: Emerson and Ned burst through the doors together to find...
Chuck!
...Chuck sitting behind Betty’s desk, covered in an A MASS OF
CRAWLING, ANXIOUS BEES.
NED (CONT’D)
I told you this was dangerous. Just because
you’re alive-again, doesn’t mean you can’t
be dead again. There’s a reason I don’t let
Digby play in traffic.
(then)
I suppose we can talk about this later.
Chuck, unable to speak, just stares at them, her finger poking
out from among the bees, toward Emerson.
Why she pointing at me?
Ned uses the coat stand to push bee-covered Chuck toward Emerson.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Why you pushing her toward me?
‘Cause you’re in front of the open door.
Emerson crosses to the balcony door and pushes it all the way
open, as Ned cautiously approaches the chair Chuck is sitting
in. He continues to push Chuck toward the balcony door.
NED (CONT’D)
Don’t offend the bees. Don’t offend the bees.
Don’t offend the bees. Don’t offend the bees.
They arrive at the open door and Chuck spits the Queen Bee out
of her mouth with a “PUHHH.” The Queen flies out and the swarm
of bees fly off of Chuck and follow their leader.
NED (CONT’D)
She’s been traumatized. Give her a hug!
Emerson takes Chuck into a reluctant hug.
Girl, what happened to you?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 41.
CONTINUED:
What happened was this:
MINUTES EARLIER - FLASHBACK
Chuck is looking at the NEWSPAPER CLIPPING of bee-bearded Young
Betty. We HEAR a low-level HUM that builds to an active
BZZZZZZZZZing. A BEE flies through FRAME. Chuck turns to see:
The Bee-Man was not composed of bees. The
drones nested around their Queen, safe inside
the Bee-Man’s mouth.
The TERRIFYING BEE-MAN, standing right behind her. His/her face
and much of his/her torso is obscured by a MASS OF CRAWLING,
ANXIOUS BEES. Chuck opens her mouth to scream and...
...the Terrifying Bee-Man SPITS SOMETHING at Chuck.
CLOSE ON - A CAGED QUEEN BEE - SLOW MOTION
A small, plastic honeycomb-shaped cage houses a Queen Bee. Cage
and Queen sail through the air toward Chuck...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But when he spat the Queen, she signaled her
drones to attack any perceived predator.
...and flies directly into her mouth.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Unlike Kentucky Fitz, Chuck kept a cool head
and an open mouth. She was not perceived as a
predator, but a nest.
THE SWARM OF BEES fly INTO Chuck’s POV, COVERING THE CAMERA.
RESUME - THE PRESENT
Ned quickly closes the door after the last of the bees escapes.
Chuck retrieves the NEWSPAPER CLIPPING of Young Betty sporting a
bee beard in front of a clapboard house numbered “88.”
Look. This is Betty Bee as a little girl.
She was either an unfortunately-hairy child...
...or Betty Bee is the Terrifying Bee-Man.
Wasn’t she with you?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 42.
CONTINUED:
She didn’t get out of the elevator with me.
She must’ve come back up here to wiggity-whack
you for being a spy.
Like she wiggity-whacked Kentucky.
Well, my wiggity wasn’t whacked. And I got
the bee-key.
That’s a house key.
I know whose house it goes to.
(re: the clapboard house)
Look at the house number. Why would Kentucky
have the key to Betty’s childhood home?
Now that we got the key, we’re gonna find out.
As Chuck followed the bee-key that was key...

scenes.heading: INT. NUNNERY - CHAPEL - CONFESSIONAL BOOTH - EARLY EVENING

lines.text: Olive slides into the booth.
...Olive Snook followed her homesick heart to
the confessional.
Forgive me, Father, for I’m going to file a
police report on all my worldly possessions.
I know that’s greedy and wrathful, but there
was a miscommunication. And now that we’re
discussing it, I don’t think I belong here.
I’m not cut from the cloth that a woman of the
cloth is cut from. My cloth is a much more
delicate fabric. It has a floral print.
Suddenly, the PARTITION SLIDES OPEN, REVEALING LILY.
A-ha! I knew you’d lapse.
You. You got some crust coming in here like
that. How long have you been lurking?
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 43.
CONTINUED:
I’ve been lurking since you walked through
those gates. Had to make sure you didn’t
get any ideas in that nubbin of yours about
leaving.
It’s your fault I’m here. You and your damn --
Hail Mary -- secrets. Spent so much time praying,
I’ve run out of things to say. I’m having awkward
silences with God. I wanna go home.
Where’s “home”? Back to slinging pies where
you spend every waking minute praying that the
man you worship might show you a sign of his
love? You can do that here. And commiserate.
These nuns aren’t my people. Unless you’re
telling me “flibbityjibbit” is a title of
respect.
You’re not even trying to enjoy yourself.
All right. They serve a nice merlot at
Eucharist.
You know things about me nobody knows. And
this place knows things about me nobody knows.
Like how you holidayed here 30 years ago and
found a baby in the cabbage patch. And by
“cabbage patch,” I mean your lady parts.
Vivian can never know about that. She
thought I was in Paris, apprenticing at a
world-class fromagerie, but I was here,
pregnant with Charlotte.
Why don’t you just tell her?
Charlotte’s father, my lover, was Vivian’s
fiancé.
You did not just tell me another secret!
You’re a home-wrecker, too. Wait. Chuck’s
father, your lover, was Vivian’s fiancé.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 44.
CONTINUED: (2)
You’re Chuck’s aunt and mother, which makes
Chuck’s father your brother? Jiminy-Crispy.
Don’t “Jiminy-Crispy” me. It’s not incest.
He was our stepbrother. We were in our
twenties when his father married our mother.
Chuck thinks her mother died during
childbirth. I mean, according to Vivian,
Chuck -- Charlotte thought her mother died
during childbirth.
It doesn’t matter what Charlotte thought.
She’s dead now. Look at you, all pious.
You’d think you’d fit right in at a nunnery.
Hell, might even do you some good.
Who are you? The “Good for Me” police?
That Epic Tanty you pitched back at the Pie
Hole wasn’t all my doing.
I admit I do have some man issues to sort out.
So sort ‘em out. Sort ‘em out right here
where men won’t be an issue. Stay as long as
you like. Until your head is clear.
And with that, Lily slowly slides the partition shut, leaving
Olive alone in the dark.
But Olive feared Lily’s idea of “as long as
you like” was considerably longer than hers.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 45.
OMIT
39 miles away, north by northeast. The
Private Detective, the Pie-Maker and Chuck
climbed a windy road to the childhood home
of Betty Bee. A home that was supposed to
be vacant.
(then)
But the home was not vacant at all.
Dark and moody, with shafts of moonlight cutting through the
room. Ned, Emerson and Chuck (in beekeeper’s suits) climb the
stairs to the second floor. Mounting the landing, Emerson, gun
drawn, sees the walls and ceiling covered in patches of hives.
Damn... Somehow a crazy cat-lady don’t seem
so crazy anymore.
So Kentucky helps Betty steal Betty’s bees,
they fake a colony collapse and get away with
conspiracy, sabotage and grand theft.
Then why would Betty kill Kentucky?
Maybe she didn’t kill Kentucky.
What do you mean? You’ve been on the trolly,
ringing the “Betty did it” bell.
That was when Betty’s bees were dead, not
stolen. She’s no longer the craziest and/or
most pissed-off person in the equation.
Who is?
My money’s on Woolsey Nicholls.
I thought he’d just send a swarm of lawyers.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 46.
CONTINUED:
If it was business, but this was personal.
You gotta be emotionally invested to put on a
swarm of bees and sting a bitch to death.
Woolsey hand-picked Kentucky to be the new
face of Betty’s Bees. Then she betrayed him.
Sabotaged his company and stole his bees and
played him like Boo Boo the fool.
BETTY (O.S.)
Boo Boo had it coming.
Emerson, Ned and Chuck all startle and SCREAM, turning to see
Betty standing in the next room, unprotected by a bee suit.
BETTY (CONT’D)
Woolsey’s conglomerate takes over Betty’s Bees,
he tells me I’m too old and slaps my name on an
inferior product. Did you know there’s now 60
percent less honey in all Betty’s Bees honey-
based products. Including honey. Fine. He
wants the company, he can have it. But I’ll be
damned if he can have my bees.
(to Chuck)
Hello, Kitty.
(to Ned)
And you. You’re not a temp. Who are you people?
We’re private investigators. We were hired by
Kentucky’s husband to find her killer.
There is no killer. That’s what the police
told me. Can’t prosecute a swarm of bees
for murder.
You can prosecute Woolsey Nicholls.
Evidently not. No weapon. No motive.
Bees were his weapon. And you know the motive.
I loved Kentucky like a sister, but if I told
the police Woolsey killed her because we were
sabotaging his company, I would go to jail a
lot longer than Woolsey ever would for murder.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 47.
CONTINUED: (2)
You might be safer in jail.
I was attacked in your office by a swarm of
bees. I think those bees were meant for you.
If you loved Kentucky like a sister, then you
have to tell the police what you know. You
can’t let Woolsey get away with murder.
Woolsey is gonna get away with murder unless
you can pull his DNA off one of those bees.
Oh. Oh.

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - WOOLSEY NICHOLLS’S OFFICE - NIGHT

lines.text: The doors burst open as Emerson (gun drawn), Ned, Chuck and
Betty ENTER. Woolsey reacts, startled behind his desk.
Please don’t stand up. Allow me to introduce
myself. Emerson Cod, private detective. I’d
like to ask you a few questions about Kentucky
Fitz’s murder and the attempted murder of
Betty Bee.
I don’t know anything about Betty, but
Kentucky wasn’t murdered. That swarm chased
her to her car, all the way from the colony.
That swarm chased her all the way from you.
And you tried to kill Betty the exact same
way, but that wasn’t Betty in her office.
Chuck holds a small evidence bag with a CAGED QUEEN BEE inside.
This is the Queen Bee cage that you spat at me
when you were covered in bees. We found it
outside Betty’s office, under a swarm.
I’m sure if we tested it for spittle, we’d
find some that belongs to you.
(voice cracking)
I have no idea what you’re talking about.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 48.
CONTINUED:
A BEE crawls out of Woolsey’s collar and buzzes into the air.
The facts were these:
FLASHBACK
Woolsey sits behind his desk, showing Kentucky the mock-up of a
Betty’s Bees product featuring Betty’s original face. He smiles
and flirts (albeit professionally), never blinking.
Woolsey Nicholls was madly in love with Kentucky
Fitz. The operative word was “madly.”
Woolsey folds over a transparency on the Betty Bee product mock-
up that covers Betty’s face with Kentucky’s.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Betty Bee was a withered hag by the mere fact
that she wasn’t Kentucky.
Kentucky forces a smile, pretending to love her face on the
Betty Bee product.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Shortly after Kentucky gratefully accepted
Woolsey’s offer to become the new face of
Betty’s Bees, he discovered her gratitude was
insincere and her intention was sabotage.
CLOSE ON - A JAR OF DEAD BEES - ANOTHER FLASHBACK
Infected bees were found in Kentucky’s
possession. She was smuggling mite-
infested bees into his new colony.
A magnifying glass MAGNIFIES a mited bee held with tweezers.
ON WOOLSEY
He sits behind his desk, brooding. CAMERA PUSHES IN on his
inscrutable expression...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Betrayed and brokenhearted, but not sloppy,
Woolsey dealt with Kentucky using a means that
would also imply accidental death.
He holds up a CAGED QUEEN BEE.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 49.
FLASHBACK - BETTY BEE’S OFFICE (RE-USE OF SCENE 49)
Chuck is looking at the NEWSPAPER CLIPPING of bee-bearded Young
Betty, her back to CAMERA so we can’t clearly see who she is.
We HEAR a low-level HUM that builds to an active BZZZZZZZZZing.
A BEE flies through FRAME.
Chuck turns to see: The TERRIFYING BEE-MAN, standing behind her.
His/her face and much of his/her torso is obscured by a MASS OF
CRAWLING, ANXIOUS BEES. Chuck opens her mouth to scream and--

scenes.heading: INT. BETTY’S BEES - WOOLSEY NICHOLLS’S OFFICE

lines.text: TWO POLICE OFFICERS pin Woolsey to his desk and cuff him.
Woolsey Nicholls confessed to the murder of
Kentucky Fitz and attempted murder of Betty Bee.
Woolsey is pulled to his feet and led out of the room. CAMERA
PUSHES ON Betty as a wry smile crawls across her cheek.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He never knew the colony collapse was a hoax
or that Betty had stolen back her bees.
BZZZ! A YELLOW NEON SIGN that reads: “HONEY HOUSE” blinks on.
Since Kentucky Fitz was like a sister to Betty
Bee, Betty Bee was like a sister to Dusty Fitz
and made him her new partner.
Betty stands proudly. She’s joined by Dusty Fitz, who holds a
framed photo of his deceased wife.
CLOSE ON:
NED stands in the middle of a library of books. Squeezing one
last tome onto an already-full shelf, he steps back, REVEALING:
The once-barren apartment has been transformed -- furniture,
paintings and SHELVES and SHELVES of BOOKS.
Realizing that his colony had not collapsed
-- but had merely expanded into His and Her
suites -- the Pie-Maker labored to make
Chuck’s suite feel like home.
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 50.
CONTINUED:
The door behind Ned CLICKS open. Chuck ENTERS, her mouth
instantly agape.
Are those my books? And my furniture... And
my special pillow. How did you...?
Welcome home.
Chuck smiles.
Ned lies awake in his bed, staring at the ceiling.
And so the Pie-Maker had come to understand
home did not mean four walls and a door you
never walked out of.
Chuck clutches her special pillow tightly, then places it at the
head of her new bed. She lies down.

scenes.heading: INT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - HALLWAY - NIGHT

lines.text: Chuck knocks on Ned’s door. He answers. She slips inside.
Home was a feeling of where you belonged.
Emerson, at his desk, puts the final touches on his pop-up book.
For Emerson Cod, home was “Lil’ GumShoe,” the
tale of a girl whose father couldn’t find her,
so she had to find him. Mr. Cod insists it’s a
work of fiction, but if published, it could
serve as a how-to manual for an audience of one.
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON THE “LIL’ GUMSHOE” COVER. Where a
MAGNIFYING GLASS highlights a thumb print and Emerson’s byline.
Olive uses a light brush to clean a truffle, smiling to herself.
For Olive Snook, home was the place she hoped
to find herself and perhaps...
PUSHING DAISIES #201 "Bzzzzzzzzz!" 09/02/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 51.
CONTINUED:
A SHADOW falls over Olive. She looks up to see a TRUFFLE-
HUNTING PIG. She’s wearing a collar that reads: “PIGBY.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...find new friends with not so many secrets.
Heya, Pigby.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - DAY

lines.text: Ned and Chuck bustle about the kitchen.
For “Lonely Tourist” Charlotte Charles, aka,
Chuck, home was where the Pie-Maker was.
CAMERA moves away from Ned to FIND one MAN (50s) in an overcoat
and a fedora, with his back to CAMERA.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And this home was a place the Pie-Maker’s
father who abandoned him would return to...
WE SLOWLY PUSH in on the man from behind, closer and closer...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...even if the Pie-Maker never knew he was
there.
